provenance: x402 specification v2 section 5.5, Settlement and Refusal Identity Invariant, as proposed in x402-foundation/x402 pull request 3776 on branch spec/settlement-refusal-identity-invariant and not on main
the gap these cover was named by ruiruii in erc-8004/erc-8004-contracts#99 on 18 October 2026: each of the four evidence layers depends on an attempt identity that none of them defines
section 5.5 closes by referring to "the normative conformance tests in the specification repository for the required negative cases"; at the time of writing those did not exist
encodes: The first of the two inverse traps: an identity that moves when the key order moves, so it came from the bytes.
description: Two arrivals of the same attempt, same decoded fields, different key order and whitespace, and two different identities. The clause says an attempt is the same attempt either way, and that this is exactly what makes settle and refusal agree. An implementation that hashes the raw body fails here.

wire_variants.note: same fields, keys in another order

limits: The two variants are asserted to carry the same decoded fields; a checker verifies that before judging, and reports not-measured when they differ.
